conviction_note: FY26 is fully pre-released (24 Sep RNS), so the move lives in the first FY27 guide and Q1 current trading including the first quantification of the 6 Oct cyber incident. The stock has given back the whole post-update rally (430p before, 508p peak, 428p sealed), so the bar has come down. Against that, ASOS sold off on both prior finals (-6.5%, -5.3%) on cautious guides, Frasers has been a net seller, and the post-update FY27 consensus is unsourced. abs_move is set on the guidance-event scale (9%), with only a mild lean up (p_up 55). The findings sum (+2.5) is larger than the scaled +0.9 because each finding is sized on its own, and the reaction history on finals pulls p_up, not the findings, toward 50.

already_public.what: FY26 (52 weeks to 30 Aug 2026) pre-released: adjusted EBITDA above the midpoint of £150-180m (more than +25% YoY, including c.£3.9m of provision releases), adjusted gross margin above 50% against a 48-50% guide, Q4 GMV low-single-digit growth, FY GMV -5%, net debt c.£110m, FCF 'slightly negative', results date 5 Nov with analyst presentation at 09:30 GMT

Cyber incident: an unauthorised push notification was sent via third-party customer-communication platforms; names and contact details may have been accessed; website and app operating normally; 'too early to quantify any potential impact on trading'. The stock fell about 10% that day (502p to 454p close)

Company-compiled consensus (9 contributors, published 21 Sep 2026, i.e. before the pre-close update): FY26 EBITDA £159m, FY27 EBITDA £177m (range £162-200m), FY27 GMV +2.2%, FY27 gross margin 49.6%, FY27 FCF £34m
ASOS promoted to the FTSE 250 effective 1 Oct 2026 (Beazley deletion); index flow already done

new_in_release.expect: First FY27 guide (adjusted EBITDA range, GMV direction, gross margin). The FY26 exit rate (Q4 GMV growth, GM >50%, about £12m annual cash savings from the warehouse sales) supports a guide at or above the stale £177m consensus. Management guided below consensus at the last two finals, though. Lean slightly up, uncertain.

Q1 FY27 current trading (Sept-Oct), the first statement on whether the cyber incident hit demand. The 6 Oct RNS reported no operational disruption, so the most likely reading is limited impact. Unknown, lean up relative to what the price has absorbed.
FY26 FCF was pre-flagged as slightly negative, below the £6m consensus. The FY27 FCF outlook against the £34m consensus is unknown, and cash has outweighed a guide before.
Cyber cost quantification, insurance recovery and any regulator (ICO) exposure. Unknown.
none expected (loss-making at PBT, no dividend)

bar: Company-compiled sell-side consensus on asosplc.com, 9 contributors, published 21 Sep 2026 (before the 24 Sep upgrade): FY27 adjusted EBITDA £177m (£162-200m), GMV +2.2%, GM 49.6%. https://www.asosplc.com/investors/consensus-estimates/ . session_check: bmo. The issuer's own notice in the 24 Sep 2026 RNS says FY26 results come 'on 5 November 2026' with 'an analyst presentation at 09:30 GMT that day', and ASOS's results-type RNS go out at 07:00 (the pre-close update was stamped 07:00 AM on Investegate). https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/asos--asc/pre-close-trading-update-/9787910
positioning_check: FCA aggregated net short 1.09% of ISC, position date 2026-09-25, down from 1.38% (covering, -0.29pp), and unchanged in the 2026-11-03 file I re-read. Not crowded. https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv . TR-1s show Frasers Group (23.37% economic interest) cutting directly held shares from 27.0m (19 Sep) to 25.0m (14 Oct). findings.finding: The cyber incident that took about 10% off the stock on 6 Oct, and roughly 15% from the post-update peak since, was a customer-communications-platform breach with no operational disruption per the company's own RNS. The results are the first chance to quantify it, and a 'no material trading impact' line would retrace part of a fall worth about £50m of market cap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One prior instance: the 6 Oct disclosure itself moved -9.6% close to close on 4.4m shares (about 20x normal volume). There is no prior results-day read on cyber.
findings.why_not_priced: The price has treated it as an open-ended M&S-style risk: the close is 428p against 502p before the incident, below the 430p pre-update level although the FY26 upgrade stands. If the market believed 'operating as normal, payment data and passwords not affected', the stock would sit nearer the 460-500p post-update range. No broker preview quantifying cyber impact was found. The risk runs the other way if Q1 trading shows customer attrition or the BBC-reported wider data set (addresses, DOB, searches) brings regulatory cost; this finding lands on the Q1 FY27 current-trading line.
findings.independence: Third-party coverage repeats the company line (ITV 8 Oct, https://www.itv.com/news/2026-10-08/asos-says-unauthorised-party-gained-access-but-payment-information-safe). Malwarebytes reports a wider stolen data set, which cuts against (https://malwarebytes.com/blog/data-breaches/2026/10/asos-breach-update-hackers-stole-customer-details-and-shopping-searches). No independent traffic or app series found.

findings.finding: The first FY27 guide starts from an FY26 exit rate (Q4 GMV growth, the first quarterly active-customer growth since Q2 FY22, GM >50%, about £12m annual cash savings from the Lichfield/Atlanta sales) that sits above the inputs of the stale FY27 consensus (EBITDA £177m, GM 49.6%, GMV +2.2%, compiled before the upgrade).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Finals with a new-year guide moved -6.54% (FY24 results, 2024-11-05) and -5.26% (FY25 results, 2025-11-21, the guide missed views). Trading updates that raised the bar moved +13.0% and +13.7%. Management has guided cautiously at finals.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus on the company's own page was collated before the 24 Sep upgrade and shows FY27 GM below the FY26 outturn. The share price has round-tripped the whole upgrade (430p to 508p to 428p), so the market is not paying for a higher FY27 base. If it were, the stock would hold the post-update range. Capped small because the post-update bar is unsourced and the company guided below views at the last two finals.
findings.independence: Shares the pre-close RNS as the base (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/asos--asc/pre-close-trading-update-/9787910). Berenberg's 750p target raise on 24 Sep points the same way (https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/share-tips/stockbroker-tips/broker-tips-asos,-on-the-beach).

findings.finding: Zalando, the closest listed European online-fashion peer, reported Q3 (Jul-Sep 2026) group GMV +7.5% with GMV up across all three consumer apps and confirmed its FY guide on 3 Nov. That points to steady European online fashion demand over ASOS's Q4 FY26 and early Q1 FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured ASOS reaction to Zalando prints. ASOS rose 2.9% on 4 Nov, the session after Zalando's release, which may be this read-across already.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced already (ASOS +2.9% on 4 Nov). This is a proxy: Zalando is continental and B2B-heavy, while ASOS is UK-led, and macro-to-company transmission is unproven. Kept small; it lands on ASOS's current-trading line.
findings.independence: None from a different source; Next's Q3 trading statement is not out yet (https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/NXT).

findings.finding: Frasers Group, the 23% holder, cut its directly held shares from 27.0m (19 Sep) to 25.0m (14 Oct), selling into the post-update rally. On 29 Oct, a week before results, it lent out 2.7m shares ('right to recall'). That leaves a seller and borrowable stock in the book into the print.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public TR-1s, and the stock's drift lower suggests the overhang is partly in the price. The FCA aggregate short (1.09%, covering) does not show the lent shares being used for a disclosed short, so the borrow may be for hedging. Kept small. Frasers' economic interest is unchanged on 29 Oct, and its sold March 2027 puts show it is willing to buy lower.
findings.independence: Frasers' earlier TR-1s (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/asos--asc/holding-s-in-company/9827999). Goldman's securities-lending position falling from 5.28% to 2.84% over October is a separate series and does not clearly point either way.

Against them stand the two negative finals reactions and Frasers' selling, so the scaled number (+0.9) is much smaller than the findings sum (+2.5).
